definition: Pinnacle means the highest point of success or achievement.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pinnacle. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pinnacle should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Being asked to design the city's new concert hall was the pinnacle of the architect's forty-year career.
A milestone only marks distance covered — a first job, a hundredth show — with the road still running on ahead; a pinnacle is where the road stops climbing.
A triumph is one great victory among the many a career may hold; a pinnacle sits above them all — the single highest achievement, with nothing left to climb beyond it.

Peak is the everyday word for a top — mountains, careers, afternoon traffic — and peaks can recur: a career may peak twice. Pinnacle is grander and admits no repeat: the single crowning achievement above which nothing stands. Every pinnacle is a peak; only one peak can be the pinnacle.

Apex is the geometry word: the highest point of a triangle, an arc, or a sales curve, stated coolly and without applause. Pinnacle carries the applause — it crowns a career or an art with a sense of glory earned. An apex is measured; a pinnacle is celebrated.
the lowest dip in a curve of fortunes
the low ground lying between two heights

Pinnacle's root — Latin pinna, 'feather, wing-tip, battlement' — never built another everyday English word; its relatives, like the botanist's pinnate leaf, stayed technical. Take the word whole: the little rooftop turret that came to mean the top of everything.
Pinnacle means the highest point of success or achievement.

The violinist had played a thousand stages, but walking out alone at the great Vienna hall — the concert every teacher had described in hushed tones since she was six — she knew she had reached the pinnacle: nothing in her art stood higher.
Pinnacle names the single topmost point, not a stretch of good years: a career holds many fine moments, but only one pinnacle — the achievement above which there is nothing left to climb.

Pinnacle crowns a career or field: the pinnacle of her profession, of the sport, of the art.
Its unit-mate zenith prefers eras and powers at their height — an empire's zenith — while pinnacle prefers a single crowning achievement.
Both allow only one: if there were two, neither would be the pinnacle.

When the dance world talks about Elena Souza, one night comes up before any other.
Her 2011 Giselle is remembered as the pinnacle of her career -- and dancers use the word deliberately, because her career had no shortage of high points.
She had won competitions at nineteen, headlined two companies, and drawn ovations on four continents.
But colleagues insist that night stood alone.
Even her later farewell tour, sold out for months, is discussed as an echo of it rather than a rival to it.
Critics who saw it describe the performance the same way: the one summit of a climbing life, above which there was simply nothing else.
